channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Russia identify cooperation areas in digitalization
item.description: Uzbekistan and Russia held a roundtable on digital transformation, exploring cooperation in digital technologies, artificial intelligence, and the digital economy. Participants discussed expanding the use of digital technologies and AI in economy, social spheres, and governance. The initiative for a joint digital ecosystem was highlighted.

item.title: President of Uzbekistan departs for Belgrade for official visit
item.description: The President of Uzbekistan, Shavkat Mirziyoyev, has departed for Serbia on an official visit at the invitation of President Aleksandar Vučić. The program includes high-level negotiations and a business forum to discuss strengthening bilateral cooperation. A package of documents is expected to be signed.

item.title: Uzbekistan enhances responsibility for nuclear safety violations
item.description: Uzbekistan's Legislative Chamber discussed amendments to laws concerning industrial, radiation, and nuclear safety. The bill aims to improve state supervision, align with international standards, and strengthen measures to prevent violations. It clarifies the powers of the Committee for Industrial, Radiation, and Nuclear Safety and the Mining Supervision Inspectorate.

item.title: Uzbekistan to mandate state registration for medical workers from 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to change medical worker licensing. From 2030, medical and pharmaceutical professionals will require state registration and independent knowledge assessment to practice. A voluntary system will be in place from 2027 to 2030. This aims to enhance the quality and safety of healthcare services.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Cabinet approves pension increase effective October 1, 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers has approved a 20% indexation of the insurance part of pensions, effective October 1, 2026. The increase will range from 1,000 to 10,000 soms. This applies to pensions granted before October 1, 2026, with a minimum total pension of 8,800 soms.

item.title: Kazakhstan tops World Nomad Games medal standings after recount
item.description: Kazakhstan secured first place in the World Nomad Games medal standings following a recount of medals won by three Kazakh athletes. The presidential press secretary congratulated Kazakhstan on their victory, emphasizing the Games' success in fostering mutual respect and unity.

item.title: Gas Extraction Begins at New 'Patron' Gas Condensate Field in Uzbekistan
item.description: Gas extraction has commenced at the new 'Patron' gas condensate field in the Mirishkor district of Qashqadaryo region, Uzbekistan. The first exploratory well was connected to the gas pipeline on September 2. The Ministry of Energy refuted claims of a gas explosion, stating the video showed the testing of the new field.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Mandate State Registration for Medical Professionals by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to introduce a state registration system for medical and pharmaceutical professionals, starting voluntarily in 2027 and becoming mandatory by 2030. An electronic registry will be created, integrating data from 16 information bases. Unregistered specialists will not be permitted to practice medicine or pharmacy.

item.title: Eurasian Development Bank Forecasts 10.2% Economic Growth for Kyrgyzstan in 2026
item.description: The Eurasian Development Bank (EDB) forecasts Kyrgyzstan's economy to grow by 10.2 percent by the end of 2026, leading regional growth. Key drivers include industrial and energy sector investments, and residential construction. Inflation is expected to reach 11.5 percent, with the national currency averaging 88 soms per dollar.

item.title: Chinese Media Reports Suspected Smuggling of 46 Tons of Raw Materials for Russian Drone Production
item.description: Chinese media reports suggest that 46 tons of raw materials, used for carbon fiber production for military drones, were secretly shipped to Russia disguised as civilian cargo. This quantity is reportedly sufficient to produce at least 1,300 military drones.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's SCNS Detains Two Customs Officers for Illegal Goods Clearance
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security (SCNS) has detained two customs officers at Osh Customs for allegedly facilitating illegal clearance of goods. The officers are accused of failing to properly inspect shipments and circumventing customs procedures, causing significant state damage.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Serbia deepen bilateral ties, RTV reports
item.description: Serbian media outlet RTV highlighted the growing relationship between Uzbekistan and Serbia, encompassing political dialogue, inter-parliamentary ties, humanitarian cooperation, and trade-economic collaboration. The report noted that bilateral relations have reached a multi-faceted partnership level, built on mutual respect and national interest alignment.

item.title: Uzbekistan to reform medical and pharmaceutical training by 2027/28
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to reform its medical training system, proposing a six-year "General Medicine" bachelor's program starting in the 2027/28 academic year. This shift aims to focus on practical skills and professional competencies, aligning with international standards. Admission quotas will be adjusted based on regional needs and specialist shortages.

item.title: Uzbekistan enhances judicial aid quality, increasing judge numbers significantly
item.description: Uzbekistan has significantly improved judicial assistance quality by increasing the number of judges. From 1,057 judges for 32 million people in 2016, the number rose to 1,731 for 39 million people today. This reform created a unified court system and specialized administrative courts for challenging state actions.

item.title: Kyrgyz President urges Ombudsperson to investigate torture allegations thoroughly
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov met with Ombudsperson Jamilya Jamanbaeva to discuss human rights protection. Japarov stressed that protecting rights is a state priority and urged the Ombudsman's office to conduct full investigations into torture allegations, defend citizens' rights, and resist pressure from law enforcement.

item.title: Combating Poverty Requires Tailored Family-Based Solutions, Uzbek President States
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev emphasized that poverty reduction requires understanding each family's specific needs and providing targeted support, not just general aid. Addressing poverty effectively involves helping families start businesses, acquire skills, and secure stable incomes through their own labor, according to a recent meeting.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan records 1,764 deaths in emergencies between 2021-2025
item.description: Kyrgyzstan experienced 283 emergency situations from 2021 to 2025, resulting in 1,764 fatalities and over 8.2 billion soms in material damage. Drowning was a significant cause, claiming 270 lives during this period. Mudflows and avalanches also caused numerous deaths.

item.title: Kazakhstan tops medal standings at World Nomad Games after recount
item.description: Kazakhstan secured first place in the overall medal standings at the VI World Nomad Games following a recalculation. The games, held in Kyrgyzstan from August 31 to September 6, 2026, concluded as a major sporting event. The press secretary of the Kyrgyz president congratulated Kazakhstan on their victory, emphasizing fair competition and mutual respect.

item.title: Navoi Seminar Focuses on Entrepreneurial Interests and Economic Development Support
item.description: A practical seminar in Navoi, attended by the Deputy Chairman of the Tax Committee, highlighted the importance of entrepreneurship for economic growth. The event emphasized creating favorable conditions for the private sector, protecting business interests, and supporting initiatives. Measures to reduce administrative barriers and foster a stable business environment were discussed.

item.title: Trial for 'Letter of 75' case continues, key figures await verdict
item.description: The Bishkek City Court held another hearing in the 'Letter of 75' case, involving former GKNB head Kamchybek Tashiev and other officials. The prosecution requested nine years imprisonment for all defendants. The next session on September 10 may see the verdict announced, following appeals against the initial four-year sentences.

item.title: Bayaut District Begins Grain Sowing Season with Focus on Agrotechnical Standards
item.description: The grain sowing season for the 2027 harvest has commenced in Bayaut district, with a practical seminar held at 'Doston Bobur' farm. Participants emphasized strict adherence to agrotechnical requirements, proper seed selection, soil preparation, timely sowing, efficient water use, and appropriate fertilizer application for high yields.

item.title: Jizzakh Province Hosts Youth Meeting and Patriotism Festival
item.description: Jizzakh Province organized a 'Leader and Youth Meeting' and 'Patriotism Festival' in Pakhtakor district to foster patriotism and responsibility among young people. Discussions covered youth life, future plans, protection from negative influences, legal and spiritual literacy, and healthy lifestyle promotion.

item.title: New electronic map presented in Dushanbe to combat traffic congestion
item.description: A new electronic map and digital applications were presented in Dushanbe to improve traffic management and reduce congestion. The initiative, discussed by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the 'Smart City' enterprise, aims to leverage modern technologies for analyzing traffic, identifying bottlenecks, and enhancing urban infrastructure efficiency.

item.title: Central Asian Sarez Lake Faces Potential Risks After Nepal Disaster
item.description: A recent disaster in Nepal, where a glacial lake outburst blocked a river causing floods, has raised concerns about similar risks in Central Asia. The incident highlights the potential dangers associated with Sarez Lake in Tajikistan, prompting renewed consideration of its vulnerabilities.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Reform Bottled Gas Supply System for Residents
item.description: Uzbekistan is set to reform its bottled gas supply system following a presentation to President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. The reforms aim to ensure timely delivery, prevent supply disruptions, and support vulnerable families, addressing current issues where some consumers face long waits and higher costs.

item.title: Tajikistan: New Sports Facilities, Poultry Farm, and School Opened in Rasht District
item.description: In honor of Tajikistan's 35th Independence Day, Rasht District inaugurated sports grounds, a poultry farm, and a new school building for 160 students. Nine kilometers of local roads were also asphalted. The projects aim to improve youth sports opportunities and local infrastructure.

item.title: Uzbek President Orders Strict Schedule for Liquefied Gas Supply
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has ordered the strict implementation of a schedule for liquefied gas supply. He also issued directives to ensure transparency in distribution and prevent artificial shortages and unjustified price increases.

item.title: Two killed in Surxondaryo after car collides with train at unguarded crossing
item.description: Two women, aged 47 and 30, died when a car collided with a train at an unguarded railway crossing in Denov district, Surxondaryo region. A two-year-old girl and the driver were injured and hospitalized. Authorities are investigating the incident, reportedly caused by driver negligence.

item.title: UN General Assembly Endorses Shift to World Map More Accurately Reflecting Continent Sizes
item.description: The UN General Assembly adopted a resolution supporting the use of maps that more accurately depict continent sizes. 164 nations, including Uzbekistan, voted in favor, while the US was the sole dissenter. The resolution encourages using Equal Earth projection maps.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets WCO Secretary General to Discuss Customs Cooperation
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with the Secretary General of the World Customs Organization. They discussed enhancing customs administration, strengthening customs authorities' capacity, and expanding practical cooperation in combating customs offenses.

item.title: Tursunzade farmers supplied over 70,000 tons of agricultural products to Tajikistan's markets
item.description: Over 70,000 tons of agricultural products were delivered from Tursunzade to various cities and regions of Tajikistan. This includes 57,562 tons of vegetables and 5,351 tons of potatoes. Harvests are continuing, with produce stored in local cold storage facilities.

item.title: Uzbekistan Appoints Ambassador to Syria
item.description: Ayubkhon Yunusov, who also serves as Uzbekistan's ambassador to Kuwait and Iraq, has been appointed as the new ambassador to Syria. This appointment fills a diplomatic role for Uzbekistan in the region.

item.title: Military parade held with 27,000 soldiers and officers for State Independence Day
item.description: A military parade involving 27,000 soldiers and officers was conducted in celebration of State Independence Day. Similar military parades also took place in various cities and districts across the country today.

item.title: Tajikistan's 35th Independence Anniversary Celebrated in Baku
item.description: A ceremony marking Tajikistan's 35th Independence Day was held in Baku on September 4, 2026, initiated by the Tajik Embassy in Azerbaijan. Officials from Azerbaijan and diplomatic representatives attended, highlighting bilateral cooperation and Tajikistan's achievements.

item.title: Uzbekistan Among Countries Selling Gold in July
item.description: In July 2026, the Central Bank of Uzbekistan sold one ton of gold, joining other central banks like Turkey and Jordan in reducing their gold reserves. China and Poland were major buyers during this period.

item.title: Astana to Host AI & Digital Bridge 2026 Forum on Artificial Intelligence
item.description: Astana will host the AI & Digital Bridge 2026 forum from October 1-3, focusing on artificial intelligence and digitalization. The event aims to connect tech leaders, investors, and innovators, following Kazakhstan's $10 billion AI and digital infrastructure agreements.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes prison for intentional damage to border fences
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has submitted a bill proposing criminal liability for intentionally damaging state border infrastructure. The draft law suggests two to five years in prison for damaging engineering structures and barriers, citing a lack of specific provisions and the risk of unauthorized crossings. Over 320 km of barriers are installed on the Kyrgyz-Tajik border.

item.title: Iran warns US of harsher response amid renewed military tensions
item.description: Iran's leadership has warned the United States of a more painful response as military confrontations between Tehran and Washington intensify. Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf urged the US to properly assess the situation. The warning comes amid renewed military tensions between the two countries.

item.title: Almaz Imangaziev Appointed Acting Labor Minister of Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Kanat Sagynbaev has been dismissed as Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Labor, Social Security, and Migration. Almaz Imangaziev, previously Deputy Foreign Minister, is now acting head of the ministry. His appointment requires approval from the Zhogorku Kenesh. Imangaziev is a career diplomat with a PhD in political science.
